riskLibrary.risk: Eye damage (retinal burn) or skin injury from above-MPE exposure
riskLibrary.controls: All above-MPE projection kept a minimum of 3 m above audience head height; beams terminated onto defined non-reflective surfaces or open sky; software zoning verified during alignment plus physical steel grating and blackened aluminium masking fixed at the aperture; reflective surfaces identified and masked during install.
riskLibrary.action: LSO verifies zones, masking and termination before doors; daily re-checks on multi-day installs

riskLibrary.risk: Static beam or uncontrolled scanning outside approved zones
riskLibrary.controls: Scan-fail protection terminates emission on scanner fault; physical masking limits output to approved zones regardless of software state; operator in constant attendance with immediate access to the emergency stop (Category 0, BS EN ISO 13850).
riskLibrary.action: E-stop and scan-fail function tested and recorded before every performance

riskLibrary.hazard: Laser fixture shifting or falling from position
riskLibrary.risk: Beam redirected outside approved zones; injury from falling equipment
riskLibrary.controls: Brackets fixed to units with hydraulic pressure plates; bracket clamped to a rated mounting bar and secured with a wrench; secondary safety bond on every flown unit; clamping tested with reasonable force once installed.
riskLibrary.action: Rigging check by LSO after install and before each performance

riskLibrary.hazard: Manual handling of equipment and cases
riskLibrary.risk: Muscular or back injury; strain carrying to rigging points up inclines or steps
riskLibrary.controls: Manual handling training; staff work in pairs of operator and assistant when rigging; loads kept within individual capability; suitable cases and trolleys used; mechanical aid used where available.
riskLibrary.action: Crew briefed at induction; supervisor monitors during load-in/out

riskLibrary.hazard: Electrical supplies to laser projectors and control
riskLibrary.risk: Electric shock or burns from faulty equipment or damaged cabling
riskLibrary.controls: Equipment visually inspected before use; damaged equipment removed from service; water-resistant supplies and housings on outdoor units; supplies via RCD protection; equipment unplugged before being worked on; temporary installations comply with the Electricity at Work Regulations 1989 / BS 7909.
riskLibrary.action: Pre-use checks at each install; defects reported to LSO

riskLibrary.risk: Trips and falls over cabling for crew, venue staff or public
riskLibrary.controls: Cabling routed away from walkways or fed through trenches; taped, matted or ramped where crossings are unavoidable; cable runs double-checked at each stage of the installation; routes agreed with site management.
riskLibrary.action: Walk-through inspection after install and before doors

riskLibrary.risk: Cuts and abrasion injuries to hands and skin from staging and truss
riskLibrary.controls: Surroundings checked before approaching; workers' gloves and long-sleeved clothing worn during rigging.

riskLibrary.hazard: Work at height during rigging or focusing
riskLibrary.risk: Falls of persons or objects from ladders, platforms or truss
riskLibrary.controls: Work at height planned and minimised; suitable access equipment used by trained personnel only; tools lanyard-secured; exclusion area maintained below overhead work per the Work at Height Regulations 2005.
riskLibrary.action: Site supervisor controls access below overhead work

riskLibrary.hazard: Working within the stage installation area
riskLibrary.risk: Crushed or broken bones and muscular injury from stage build activity
riskLibrary.controls: No operators or assistants enter the stage area until given express permission by stage management; safe working area maintained; high-visibility clothing where required by site rules.
riskLibrary.action: Coordination with stage manager before each work period

riskLibrary.hazard: High sound pressure levels during events
riskLibrary.controls: All crew have dedicated moulded ear plugs or are supplied disposable plugs for each shift; hearing protection checked before approaching high-volume areas.
riskLibrary.action: Checked at induction and before each show

riskLibrary.risk: Unsafe behaviour, impaired operation of laser systems
riskLibrary.controls: No crew member may drink alcohol within 24 hours of operating, or 12 hours of handling/rigging equipment; instant dismissal from site of any intoxicated staff.
riskLibrary.action: Enforced by site lead; zero-tolerance policy

riskLibrary.risk: Dangerous operation or unsafe practice when tired
riskLibrary.controls: Mandatory minimum 8-hour break between operation and any other set task; staff check in and out of shifts via group messenger; alertness confirmed before dismantling begins.
riskLibrary.action: Site lead confirms rest periods before de-rig

riskLibrary.hazard: Audience aggression, encroachment or crowd surge
riskLibrary.risk: Damage or displacement of equipment; injury to operators or public; beam zones compromised
riskLibrary.controls: Equipment positioned behind barriers or out of public reach where practicable; on any loss of control on site the operator cuts emission via the e-stop and awaits the all-clear; security informed and re-enable only on LSO authorisation.
riskLibrary.action: Show-stop procedure briefed to all operators

riskLibrary.risk: Wind loading on rigging, water ingress, unsafe working conditions; beam refraction/scatter changes
riskLibrary.controls: Weather forecast monitored; outdoor units IP-rated or protected; work at height and rigging suspended above safe wind speeds; display suspended if conditions render it unsafe; equipment electrically isolated during electrical storms.
riskLibrary.action: LSO/site lead reviews conditions at each work period

riskLibrary.hazard: Laser emission into open airspace (outdoor, sky-terminating)
riskLibrary.risk: Dazzle or distraction of aircraft crew
riskLibrary.controls: CAA notified per CAP 736 (DAP 1918 / online portal); distance to nearest aerodrome assessed against CAP 736 restriction zones; beams elevated above horizontal only within the notified arrangement; named Display Operator with immediate termination capability on duty throughout; display terminated immediately on any ATC or event-control request.
riskLibrary.action: CAA notification reference recorded in this document before the event

riskLibrary.hazard: Unauthorised access to or operation of laser equipment
riskLibrary.risk: Uncontrolled emission causing exposure of any person
riskLibrary.controls: Key control by the LSO; keys removed and equipment disabled whenever unattended; controlled area around projectors restricted to authorised personnel; laser warning signage displayed at access points.
riskLibrary.action: LSO holds keys; checked at every departure from the control position

boilerplate.scopeTemplate: This document sets out the laser safety arrangements, risk assessment and method statement for the laser display provided by {{company}} at {{eventName}}{{venuePart}}. It covers the delivery, installation, alignment, programming, operation and removal of the laser display equipment listed herein, by the personnel named herein. It is valid only for the event, venue, equipment and personnel stated; any change requires review and re-issue by the Laser Safety Officer.
boilerplate.lsoResponsibilities:
In accordance with PLASA guidance, Paradox State International Ltd appoints a named Laser Safety Officer (LSO) for every installation. The LSO holds executive, not merely advisory, responsibility for laser safety: they evaluate and manage the laser risks, approve projector positions, zoning, masking and programming, carry out and record alignment and pre-show checks, and have absolute authority to suspend or terminate laser emission at any time without reference to any other party. No change to projector positions, output power, effects programming or beam zones may be made without the LSO’s agreement.

Laser projectors are operated only by trained operators named in this document. A competent operator remains in attendance at the laser control position, with an unobstructed view of the beam paths and immediate access to the emergency stop, at all times when laser emission is possible.

The client / event organiser provides site information, integrates this RAMS into the event safety plan, maintains agreed audience barriers and crowd management, and communicates the show-stop procedure. The venue advises of reflective surfaces, rigging limitations and house emergency procedures. Responsibility for laser safety is allocated between the parties before the display and is not assumed by default.
boilerplate.nohdStatement: The Nominal Ocular Hazard Distance (NOHD), the distance from the projector within which direct, reflected or scattered emission exceeds the applicable maximum permissible exposure (MPE), has been established for each projector at its show settings and is stated in the equipment inventory where calculated, or held on file and available on request (calculation sheets appended where produced). Except where an engineered audience-scanning safety case is expressly set out in this document, no emission exceeding the MPE is accessible at any position that the audience or public can occupy. In accordance with PLASA guidance, above-MPE beams and effects are kept not less than 3 m vertically above and 2.5 m laterally from any audience-accessible position (6 m vertically for any unsupervised installation); any deviation from these separations is supported by a detailed exposure assessment recorded in this document. Potentially specular or reflective surfaces within beam paths (mirrors, glazing, mirror balls, polished trussing, water) are identified during installation and eliminated, masked or assessed against the MPE.
boilerplate.controlledAreas: A laser controlled area is established around each projector and any area in which above-MPE beams are accessible. Access is restricted to authorised, safety-briefed personnel under the control of the LSO; laser warning signage compliant with PD IEC TR 60825-3:2022 is displayed at access points. Projectors are rigidly mounted with secondary safeties so that they cannot be displaced or redirected by vibration or impact. Beam output is constrained to the approved zones by software zoning verified during alignment and by physical masking or aperture plates at the projector, so that no software or scanner failure can direct emission outside the approved zones. Every static beam path terminates on a defined non-reflective, non-flammable surface, or into open sky in accordance with the aviation safety section of this document.
boilerplate.audienceScanningNo: Audience scanning: NO. No laser effects are deliberately directed into any area occupied by, or accessible to, the audience or public. All effects terminate above or away from audience-accessible positions in accordance with the separation distances stated in this document. No audience-accessible position lies within the NOHD of any projector under normal or foreseeable fault conditions.
boilerplate.audienceScanningYes: Audience scanning: YES, with an engineered safety case. Deliberate audience exposure is designed and verified in accordance with PLASA guidance and PD IEC TR 60825-3:2022. Exposure at the closest point of audience access has been calculated and verified by on-site measurement through a 7 mm aperture, under normal operation and simulated failure conditions, and does not exceed the applicable MPE (taken as 10 W/m² for 400–700 nm on a minimum 10-second time base{{childrenClause}}). Scan-failure detection hardware terminates emission on scanner fault such that no single-component failure can produce an accessible above-MPE beam. Pulsed lasers are never used for audience scanning. Measurement records form part of this document.
boilerplate.audienceScanningYesChildrenClause: , reduced by a factor of 10 below 500 nm as the performance is intended for children
boilerplate.diffractionNo: Audience exposure from diffraction effects: NO. No diffraction gratings or beam-splitting effects are directed toward audience-accessible positions.
boilerplate.diffractionYes: Audience exposure from diffraction effects: YES. Diffracted orders accessible to the audience have been measured below the applicable MPE; measurement records form part of this document.
boilerplate.alignmentProcedure:
Alignment is the highest-risk phase of the installation and is carried out only by trained personnel under the direct control of the LSO. The venue is cleared, or access to the affected areas restricted, before alignment begins. Alignment is performed at the minimum practicable output using single-beam/static test patterns; personnel within the controlled area wear laser protective eyewear of appropriate optical density for the wavelengths in use. Each beam path is physically walked and confirmed to terminate on its designated surface; reflective surfaces are identified and eliminated or masked; software zones and physical masks are then set and verified against the approved zone plan. Alignment is completed and recorded before the public is admitted.

Before each performance the LSO completes and records pre-show checks (the Display Safety Record), including: projector mounting and secondary safeties; alignment unchanged; masking in place; zone/mask verification; scan-fail function; emergency stop function; key control; signage and controlled-area integrity. Lasers are disabled, keys removed and held by the LSO whenever equipment is unattended. Daily alignment checks are made for multi-day installations, and any change to the installation requires the LSO’s agreement and a recorded re-check.
boilerplate.eStopSpec:
The emergency stop function is a CATEGORY 0 stop, implemented by the engagement and disengagement of the 230 VAC / 16 A power feed via a 25 A solid-state relay hard-lined from the FOH control position. After actuation of the emergency stop actuator, hazardous operation of the equipment is stopped without creating additional hazards and without further intervention by any person.

Stop category 0 (stopping by immediate removal of power to the laser(s)) is applied in accordance with BS EN ISO 13850 (in conjunction with the stop-category definitions of BS EN 60204-1). Once active operation of the emergency stop device has ceased following an emergency stop command, the effect of the command is sustained until it is manually reset. Reset is possible only at the location where the command was initiated, and the reset does not restart the equipment but only permits restarting.

The emergency stop provision forms part of the control-system integrity measures recommended by PD IEC TR 60825-3:2022; its function is tested and recorded as a pre-show check before every performance, with all unit shutters fully raised.
boilerplate.eStopSpecDigital:
The emergency stop function is a CATEGORY 0 stop, implemented digitally: actuation of the emergency stop control removes power from the laser emission stages of every projector via the units' onboard safety protocol, terminating emission immediately, without creating additional hazards and without further intervention by any person. The digital emergency stop path is independent of the show-control software, so a software or showfile fault cannot prevent actuation.

Stop category 0 (stopping by immediate removal of power to the laser emission stages) is applied in accordance with BS EN ISO 13850 (in conjunction with the stop-category definitions of BS EN 60204-1). Once active operation of the emergency stop device has ceased following an emergency stop command, the effect of the command is sustained until it is manually reset by the operator at the control position; the reset does not restart emission but only permits restarting.

The emergency stop provision forms part of the control-system integrity measures recommended by PD IEC TR 60825-3:2022; its function is tested and recorded as a pre-show check before every performance, with all unit shutters fully raised.
boilerplate.emergencyProcedures:
Show stop. Laser emission can be terminated immediately at any time by the operator’s emergency stop (Category 0 stop to BS EN ISO 13850, removing power to emission), and will be terminated at once on: any suspected exposure of any person to an above-MPE beam; displacement or suspected displacement of any projector; failure of scan-fail, masking or zoning; instruction from the LSO, event safety management or emergency services; encroachment of any person into a beam zone or controlled area; and, for outdoor displays, any request under the aviation arrangements or weather rendering the display unsafe. The display resumes only on the LSO’s authorisation after the cause is identified, corrected and re-checked.

Suspected eye exposure. Emission is stopped immediately; the affected person is advised not to rub the eye and is referred the same day for ophthalmological examination, regardless of symptoms. The incident is recorded and investigated by the LSO and reported under RIDDOR 2013 where applicable; equipment and programming are quarantined pending investigation.

Fire, evacuation and first aid follow the venue/event procedures, with which our crew are inducted on arrival. On evacuation the operator terminates emission and isolates power before leaving the control position, if safe to do so.
boilerplate.aviationSafety: This display projects laser light into open airspace and is managed in accordance with CAA CAP 736 (“Operation of Directed Light, Fireworks, Toy Balloons and Sky Lanterns within UK Airspace”, 3rd Issue, February 2011). CAA Airspace Regulation is notified via form DAP 1918 / the CAA online portal, with a target of 28 days’ notice and in no case less than 7 days; the notification reference and any NOTAM action are recorded in this document. The site’s distance from the nearest aerodrome reference point and extended runway centreline has been assessed against the CAP 736 restriction zones (3 NM of an ARP; 10 NM along the extended runway centreline and 500 m either side). Where the display falls within these zones, beams are prevented from illuminating the affected airspace or a direct telephone/radio link is maintained between the nominated Display Operator and the relevant air traffic control authority so that the display can be terminated immediately on request. A named Display Operator with immediate termination capability is on duty throughout. No beam will be directed at any aircraft: we recognise the offences under Article 225 of the Air Navigation Order 2016 (shining a light at an aircraft so as to dazzle or distract the pilot), Article 240 (endangering an aircraft) and the Laser Misuse (Vehicles) Act 2018.
boilerplate.aviationPermanentSite: As this installation is in place for more than 30 days it is treated as a permanent site under CAP 736 Chapter 4, with Local Planning Authority and CAA consultation and publication in UK AIP ENR 5.3.

siteSafety.electrical: Electrical safety. Temporary electrical installations and distribution comply with the Electricity at Work Regulations 1989 and BS 7909; supplies to laser and control equipment are RCD-protected; equipment is visually inspected before use and removed from service if damaged.
siteSafety.workAtHeight: Work at height. Where rigging or focusing requires work at height it is planned, minimised and carried out by trained personnel using suitable access equipment in accordance with the Work at Height Regulations 2005; every flown projector carries a rated secondary safety bond.
siteSafety.manualHandling: Manual handling. Loads are assessed; suitable cases, trolleys and team lifts are used; crew work within their individual capability.
siteSafety.cables: Cable management. Cable runs are routed away from walkways or protected by taping, matting or ramps, and are re-checked at each stage of the installation.
siteSafety.haze: Haze and smoke. Where haze or smoke is used to render beams visible it is provided and operated under the responsibility stated in the event details; fluid safety data sheets are available on request and ventilation follows venue arrangements.
siteSafety.fire: Fire. Beam paths terminate on non-flammable surfaces; projectors and dimming equipment are kept clear of combustible materials; crew are inducted in venue fire and evacuation procedures.
siteSafety.ppe: PPE. Workers’ gloves and long-sleeved clothing are worn for rigging; laser protective eyewear of appropriate optical density is worn within controlled areas during alignment only (eyewear is not a substitute for engineering controls during the show); moulded or disposable hearing protection is used in high-volume areas.
siteSafety.weather: Weather (outdoor events). Forecasts are monitored; rigging and work at height are suspended above safe wind speeds; outdoor units are IP-rated or protected from water ingress; the display is suspended if conditions render it unsafe.

methodSteps: Arrival and induction: crew sign in with site/event management, receive the site induction and confirm first-aid, fire and evacuation arrangements. Appropriate clothing and PPE are checked before any equipment leaves the transport.
Coordination: contact is made with the FOH lighting director / production manager to confirm it is safe to proceed with placing equipment. No crew enter the stage area until given express permission.
Unload and distribution: units are placed vertically below their positions on the stage lighting plot, working in pairs within individual capability.
Control infrastructure: control cabling is measured and run between the units and FOH; the emergency stop is installed and tested at its designated FOH location. {{eStopSentence}}
Power and data: power and control are distributed from stage left to stage right; all cabling is securely rigged, taped or matted in place and double-checked.
Mounting: units are mounted with brackets clamped to rated mounting bars, secured with a wrench and fitted with secondary safeties; clamping is tested with reasonable force.
E-stop verification: a full emergency-stop test is carried out with all unit shutters fully raised, and the result recorded.

Zoning and alignment: technicians and staff on site are warned before laser zoning starts. Steel shuttering is fastened at the midpoint of the aperture and units are zoned individually at 5% output power, with blackened aluminium masking applied to constrain each zone horizontally and the 3 mm steel grating limiting vertical scanning, in accordance with the alignment procedure in this document.
Programming and verification: software zones and masks are verified against the approved zone plan; showfiles are checked on the primary and backup control systems.
Pre-show checks: the Display Safety Record checks are completed and recorded before doors; the LSO authorises the display.

Show operation: a trained operator remains at the control position with an unobstructed view of the beam paths and immediate access to the e-stop throughout; the show-stop procedure applies at all times. At no point during operation is the audience scanned{{scanningException}}.
Shutdown and security: after each performance emission is disabled, keys are removed and held by the LSO, and equipment is left secured.

De-rig and load-out: dismantling begins only when crew alertness is confirmed after the mandatory rest period; equipment is inspected, packed and loaded following the same manual-handling and coordination controls as the load-in.
boilerplate.eStopSentenceHardline: All units are powered via the FOH hard-line E-Stop so that laser shutdown is instant in an emergency.
boilerplate.eStopSentenceDigital: All units are controlled via a digital E-Stop (with the projectors’ internal power removed on activation via the onboard protocol) so that laser shutdown is instant in an emergency.
boilerplate.scanningExceptionYes: except as set out in the engineered audience-scanning safety case in this document
boilerplate.complianceStatement:
Paradox State International Ltd operates in accordance with its duties under the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974, in particular sections 2 and 3 (duties to employees and to persons not in our employment, including audience members and venue staff) and, as a designer and builder of laser display equipment, section 6; and with regulation 3 of the Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations 1999. Work equipment is provided and maintained in accordance with the Provision and Use of Work Equipment Regulations 1998, and temporary electrical installations comply with the Electricity at Work Regulations 1989.

Exposure to laser radiation is managed under the Control of Artificial Optical Radiation at Work Regulations 2010 (SI 2010/1140). In accordance with regulations 3 and 4, exposure levels have been assessed and, where necessary, calculated or measured against the applicable exposure limit values, and risks are reduced to as low a level as is reasonably practicable. All laser projectors used are classified in accordance with BS EN 60825-1:2014+A11:2021 as stated in the equipment inventory.

Displays are planned, installed, aligned and operated in accordance with PLASA “Safety of Display Lasers” (1st Edition, April 2016), the industry guidance produced with the assistance of the Health and Safety Executive and Public Health England and referenced by HSE as the successor to the withdrawn HS(G)95, and with PD IEC TR 60825-3:2022, “Safety of laser products, Part 3: Guidance for laser displays and shows”. Where applicable, the Purple Guide chapter on special effects and, for outdoor displays, CAA CAP 736, the Air Navigation Order 2016 (articles 225 and 240) and the Laser Misuse (Vehicles) Act 2018 are also complied with.
boilerplate.insuranceBlurb: Evidence of insurance is provided by reproduction of the company’s certificate(s) of insurance in full, appended to and forming part of this document. Policy details are as stated on the certificate itself; no summary is substituted for it. Operators hold their own public liability insurance for laser operation where stated.
boilerplate.signOffText: This Risk Assessment and Method Statement has been prepared and approved by the persons named below and is valid only for the event, venue, equipment and personnel stated. Any change to equipment, positions, programming, venue layout or personnel requires review and re-issue.
boilerplate.briefingText: Each crew member signs below to confirm they have read, understood and will comply with this RAMS, including the alignment procedure, controlled areas, show-stop and emergency arrangements.
boilerplate.effectsTemplate: The show will be lissajous sheets of light, varying in colour and concentration. There will be NO straight beams used on site; these are disabled digitally within the control software. Pangolin Beyond will be used as primary control on a Lenovo laptop, and in the rare event of failure a backup control PC will be on site with a duplicate of the showfile. The desired effect is to create a ceiling of lissajous effects a minimum of 3 m above the height of the crowd, terminating {{termination}}.
boilerplate.unitsControlTemplate: The units being used are {{unitSummary}}. They will be controlled via Pangolin Beyond using {{controlRuns}}. Output is constrained by software zoning verified at alignment, plus physical steel shuttering and blackened aluminium masking fixed at each aperture.

hk.scopeTemplate: This document sets out the laser safety arrangements, risk assessment and method statement for the laser display provided by {{company}} at {{eventName}}{{venuePart}}. It covers the delivery, installation, alignment, programming, operation and removal of the laser display equipment listed herein, by the personnel named herein. It is prepared to support the event organiser's application for a Temporary Places of Public Entertainment (TPPE) licence, in which the laser operation is declared, the venue's prior approval of the laser effect, and the EMSD on-site inspection of the installed equipment; it forms part of the event safety documentation. It is valid only for the event, venue, equipment and personnel stated; any change requires review and re-issue by the Laser Safety Officer.
hk.lsoResponsibilities:
In accordance with the EMSD Laser Safety Guidance Notes and PLASA guidance, Paradox State International Ltd appoints a named Laser Safety Officer (LSO) for every installation. The LSO holds executive, not merely advisory, responsibility for laser safety: they evaluate and manage the laser risks, approve projector positions, zoning, masking and programming, carry out and record alignment and pre-show checks, attend the EMSD inspection and demonstration, and have absolute authority to suspend or terminate laser emission at any time without reference to any other party. No change to projector positions, output power, effects programming or beam zones may be made without the LSO's agreement.

Laser projectors are operated only by trained operators named in this document. A competent operator remains in attendance at the laser control position, with an unobstructed view of the whole display area and immediate access to the emergency stop, at all times when laser emission is possible.

The event organiser, as TPPE licence applicant, provides site information, integrates this RAMS into the event safety plan and the licence application, maintains agreed audience barriers and crowd management, and communicates the show-stop procedure. The venue (AsiaWorld-Expo Management Ltd) advises of reflective surfaces, rigging limitations, house rules and emergency procedures, and gives prior approval for the laser effect. Responsibility for laser safety is allocated between the parties before the display and is not assumed by default.
hk.controlledAreas: A laser controlled area is established around each projector and any area in which above-MPE beams are accessible, and the boundary of the laser display area is defined on the effect layout appended to this document. Access is restricted to authorised, safety-briefed personnel under the control of the LSO; laser warning signage compliant with IEC TR 60825-3:2022 is displayed at access points. Projectors are rigidly mounted with secondary safeties so that they cannot be displaced or redirected by vibration or impact. Beam output is constrained to the approved zones by software zoning verified during alignment and by physical masking or aperture plates at the projector (black-finished steel or aluminium, as recommended in Part 4 of the EMSD Guidance Notes), so that no software or scanner failure can direct emission outside the approved zones. Every static beam path terminates on a defined non-reflective, non-flammable surface within the display area boundary; no emission leaves the venue.
hk.audienceScanningYes: Audience scanning: YES, with an engineered safety case. Deliberate audience exposure is designed and verified in accordance with IEC TR 60825-3:2022 and PLASA guidance. Exposure at the closest point of audience access has been calculated and verified by on-site measurement through a 7 mm aperture, under normal operation and simulated failure conditions, and does not exceed the applicable MPE (taken as 10 W/m² for 400 to 700 nm on a minimum 10-second time base{{childrenClause}}). Scan-failure detection hardware terminates emission on scanner fault such that no single-component failure can produce an accessible above-MPE beam. Pulsed lasers are never used for audience scanning. Measurement records form part of this document and are made available to EMSD at inspection.
hk.eStopSpec:
The emergency stop function is a CATEGORY 0 stop, implemented by the engagement and disengagement of the 220 V AC single-phase power feed to the projector(s) via a solid-state relay hard-lined from the operator's control position. After actuation of the emergency stop actuator, hazardous operation of the equipment is stopped without creating additional hazards and without further intervention by any person.

Stop category 0 (stopping by immediate removal of power to the laser(s)) is applied in accordance with ISO 13850 (in conjunction with the stop-category definitions of IEC 60204-1). Once active operation of the emergency stop device has ceased following an emergency stop command, the effect of the command is sustained until it is manually reset. Reset is possible only at the location where the command was initiated, and the reset does not restart the equipment but only permits restarting.

The emergency stop provision is the emergency cut-off called for in Part 4 of the EMSD Laser Safety Guidance Notes and forms part of the control-system integrity measures recommended by IEC TR 60825-3:2022; its function is tested and recorded as a pre-show check before every public session, with all unit shutters fully raised.
hk.eStopSpecDigital:
The emergency stop function is a CATEGORY 0 stop, implemented digitally: actuation of the emergency stop control removes power from the laser emission stages of every projector via the units' onboard safety protocol, terminating emission immediately, without creating additional hazards and without further intervention by any person. The digital emergency stop path is independent of the show-control software, so a software or showfile fault cannot prevent actuation.

Stop category 0 (stopping by immediate removal of power to the laser emission stages) is applied in accordance with ISO 13850 (in conjunction with the stop-category definitions of IEC 60204-1). Once active operation of the emergency stop device has ceased following an emergency stop command, the effect of the command is sustained until it is manually reset by the operator at the control position; the reset does not restart emission but only permits restarting.

The emergency stop provision is the emergency cut-off called for in Part 4 of the EMSD Laser Safety Guidance Notes and forms part of the control-system integrity measures recommended by IEC TR 60825-3:2022; its function is tested and recorded as a pre-show check before every public session, with all unit shutters fully raised.
hk.emergencyProcedures:
Show stop. Laser emission can be terminated immediately at any time by the operator's emergency stop (Category 0 stop to ISO 13850, removing power to emission), and will be terminated at once on: any suspected exposure of any person to an above-MPE beam; displacement or suspected displacement of any projector or of the termination screen; failure of scan-fail, masking or zoning; instruction from the LSO, the organiser's event management, the venue, the licensing authorities or emergency services; and encroachment of any person into a beam zone or controlled area. The display resumes only on the LSO's authorisation after the cause is identified, corrected and re-checked.

Suspected eye exposure. Emission is stopped immediately; the affected person is advised not to rub the eye and is referred the same day for ophthalmological examination, regardless of symptoms. The incident is recorded and investigated by the LSO, reported at once to the event organiser and the venue under their incident procedures, and notified to the Labour Department where required under the Occupational Safety and Health Ordinance (Cap. 509) and the Employees' Compensation Ordinance (Cap. 282); equipment and programming are quarantined pending investigation.

Fire, evacuation and first aid follow the venue's house procedures and the organiser's event safety plan, with which our crew are inducted on arrival; the Hong Kong emergency number is 999. On evacuation the operator terminates emission and isolates power before leaving the control position, if safe to do so.
hk.aviationSafety: This display projects laser light into open airspace. The venue lies beside Hong Kong International Airport, so no outdoor emission takes place until the arrangement has been agreed in writing with the Civil Aviation Department and the venue, with regard to the Hong Kong Airport (Control of Obstructions) Ordinance, and any conditions they set are recorded in this document. A named Display Operator with immediate termination capability is on duty throughout, and the display is terminated at once on any request from air traffic control, the venue or event control. No beam will be directed at any aircraft: exhibiting a light that endangers an aircraft in flight is an offence under the Air Navigation (Hong Kong) Order 1995.
hk.aviationPermanentSite: As this installation is in place for an extended period, the arrangement is agreed with the Civil Aviation Department and the venue for its full duration.

siteSafety.electrical: Electrical safety. Temporary electrical installations comply with the Electricity Ordinance (Cap. 406) and the Electricity (Wiring) Regulations (Cap. 406E) and with the venue's rules: at AsiaWorld-Expo, power installations are completed by a registered electrical worker and a Work Completion Certificate (Form WR1) is submitted through the organiser. Laser and control equipment connects only to the socket outlet supplied for the display by the venue's official electrical contractor (220 V, 50 Hz, RCD-protected); the contractor makes no fixed wiring alterations. Equipment is visually inspected before use and removed from service if damaged.
siteSafety.workAtHeight: Work at height. Where rigging or focusing requires work at height it is planned, minimised and carried out by trained personnel under the Occupational Safety and Health Ordinance (Cap. 509) and the venue's rules: no ladder over 2 m and no wooden or modified ladders; a proper working platform with a valid safety certificate (Form 5) and a full-body harness are used for work above 2 m; every flown projector carries a rated secondary safety bond. Any item suspended from the venue ceiling is rigged by the venue's rigging service to its suspension points; the venue's thresholds for a Registered Structural Engineer's report (including any suspended item over 100 kg) are checked with the venue in advance, and nothing is suspended without the organiser's and venue's written agreement.
siteSafety.manualHandling: Manual handling. Loads are assessed; suitable cases, trolleys and team lifts are used; crew work within their individual capability. Goods are moved on rubber-wheeled trolleys along the venue's paved routes, with floor protection where the venue requires it, and never through guest lifts or escalators.
siteSafety.cables: Cable management. Cable runs are routed through venue trenches or tunnels where available, otherwise protected by tape, matting or ramps; no cable crosses a main aisle; runs are re-checked at each stage of the installation and agreed with the organiser's floor manager.
siteSafety.haze: Haze and smoke. The laser contractor does not use haze or smoke unless stated in the event details. Where haze is used it is a venue-approved special effect at AsiaWorld-Expo: its use is declared to the venue and, through the organiser, to the Fire Services Department in advance; only water-based fluid with a safety data sheet is used; the venue's arrangements for its fire detection system are followed.
siteSafety.fire: Fire. Beam paths terminate on non-flammable, non-reflective surfaces; projectors and power equipment are kept clear of combustible materials; fire service installations, exits and escape routes are kept accessible at all times; no hot work is carried out; crew are inducted in the venue's fire and evacuation procedures, which reflect the Fire Services Department's requirements for the licensed premises (PPA/106).
siteSafety.ppe: PPE. Workers' gloves and long-sleeved clothing are worn for rigging; safety footwear and a reflective vest are worn during move-in and move-out and in any area with moving vehicles, in line with the venue's dress rules; laser protective eyewear of appropriate optical density is worn within controlled areas during alignment only (eyewear is not a substitute for engineering controls during the show); hearing protection is used in high-volume areas.

methodSteps: Arrival and site registration: crew register with the organiser and AsiaWorld-Expo security, obtain the required wristbands or badges, receive the site induction and confirm first-aid, fire and evacuation arrangements. Appropriate clothing and PPE are checked before any equipment leaves the transport.

Coordination: contact is made with the organiser's production manager and, where required, the venue's event manager to confirm that the venue's prior approval for the laser effect and the electrical supply are in place and that it is safe to proceed. No crew enter the build area until given express permission.

Unload and distribution: equipment enters via the designated loading bay under the venue's vehicle-staging rules and is moved on rubber-wheeled trolleys along paved routes to the display position, working in pairs within individual capability.

Termination surface and mounting: the projection screen or scrim frame is erected and made stable on its own base or rigging, with the non-reflective backdrop and the controlled area behind it established before any projector is positioned. Projectors are mounted on rated brackets or stands, secured with a wrench and fitted with secondary safeties where flown; clamping is tested with reasonable force.

Power and control: the projectors connect only to the socket outlet supplied by the venue's official electrical contractor; control cabling is run between the projectors and the operator's control position, with all cabling taped, matted or ramped and double-checked. The emergency stop is installed and tested at the control position. {{eStopSentence}}
E-stop verification: a full emergency-stop test is carried out with all unit shutters fully raised, and the result recorded.

Zoning and alignment: the area is cleared of the public and other contractors are warned before laser zoning starts. Units are zoned individually at minimum output, with black-finished physical masking applied at the aperture so that no emission can leave the approved zone, in accordance with the alignment procedure in this document.
Programming and verification: software zones and masks are verified against the approved effect layout; showfiles are checked on the primary and backup control systems.

Inspection: the installation is presented for the EMSD on-site inspection and demonstration of the laser display before the display commences, and for any inspection by the organiser, the venue or the other licensing departments, with the LSO in attendance and this document available on site. Any recommendation made at inspection is implemented and, if required, a re-inspection is arranged before the display goes public.

Pre-show checks: the Display Safety Record checks, including the functional check of every safety device, are completed and recorded before the public is admitted to each session; the LSO authorises the display.

Show operation: a trained operator remains at the control position with an unobstructed view of the whole display area and immediate access to the e-stop throughout; the show-stop procedure applies at all times. At no point during operation is the audience scanned{{scanningException}}.
Shutdown and security: after each session emission is disabled, keys are removed and held by the LSO, and equipment is left secured within the controlled area or removed from the hall.

De-rig and load-out: dismantling begins only when crew alertness is confirmed after the mandatory rest period; equipment is inspected, packed and removed via the loading bay following the same manual-handling, vehicle-staging and coordination controls as the load-in.
hk.complianceStatement:
Paradox State International Ltd is a United Kingdom company providing this display as a specialist contractor in the Hong Kong SAR. It works in accordance with the Occupational Safety and Health Ordinance (Cap. 509) and the Occupational Safety and Health Regulation (Cap. 509A), which place general duties on employers, occupiers and persons carrying out work to ensure, so far as is reasonably practicable, the safety and health of employees and of other persons at the workplace, including audience members, venue staff and other contractors. Work equipment is provided and maintained in safe condition, and temporary electrical arrangements comply with the Electricity Ordinance (Cap. 406) and the Electricity (Wiring) Regulations (Cap. 406E).

The display takes place in a temporary place of public entertainment licensed under the Places of Public Entertainment Ordinance (Cap. 172), under which a laser projection display is entertainment. The laser operation is declared in the organiser's TPPE licence application to the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department together with the Display Laser Information required by Section 6 of the FEHD application guide, and this document, the effect layout and the equipment particulars are provided to the organiser, the venue and, on request, the licensing authority and the departments it consults (the Electrical and Mechanical Services Department, the Fire Services Department, the Buildings Department and the Police) in support of that application and of the venue's prior approval of the effect. The installed equipment is presented to EMSD for on-site inspection and demonstration before the display commences, and any conditions attached to the licence, the inspection or the venue's approval are complied with.

Exposure to laser radiation is assessed against the maximum permissible exposure limits of IEC 60825-1, and all laser projectors used are classified in accordance with that standard as stated in the equipment inventory. The display is planned, installed, aligned and operated in accordance with Part 4 of the EMSD Laser Safety Guidance Notes for Industry, Display and Entertainment (2005), which reproduces the UK HSE guidance HS(G)95 for display lasers, with IEC TR 60825-3:2022, Safety of laser products, Part 3: Guidance for laser displays and shows, and with PLASA Safety of Display Lasers (1st Edition, April 2016), the current successor to HS(G)95, applied as the industry code of practice. The company also applies its home framework, the Control of Artificial Optical Radiation at Work Regulations 2010, to every display as a matter of good practice.
hk.insuranceBlurb: Evidence of insurance is provided by reproduction of the company's certificate(s) of insurance in full, appended to and forming part of this document. Policy details, including the territorial limits applying to work in the Hong Kong SAR, are as stated on the certificate and policy schedule; no summary is substituted for them. Any cover required by the venue or the organiser beyond the company's own policy is arranged through the organiser and confirmed separately.

authorityInfoSheet.title: Display laser information for the licensing authorities
authorityInfoSheet.intro: The Food and Environmental Hygiene Department's TPPE application (form FEHB104, Annex III, Display Laser Information, and Section 6 of the FEHD application guide) and the EMSD on-site inspection call for the particulars below. They are set out here so that the organiser can transcribe them into the application and EMSD can check them against the installed equipment.
authorityInfoSheet.note: Beam divergence is stated in milliradians in the inventory and in radians here (1 mrad = 0.001 radian). The sketch plan required by Annex III (locations of the laser equipment, beam stops, control position, beam paths and patterns, reflective surfaces, barriers and the boundary of the laser display area) is the effect layout appended to this document. The demonstration that irradiance outside the boundary of the laser display area is below the MPE is given in the exposure assessment and effects sections. Equipment catalogue: the technical sheet is appended.
